correctness.rationale: The rank-one map \(N_c(z,y)=(c f(y)z_0,0)\) satisfies \(N_c^2=0\), so \(T_c^{-1}=I+N_c\). Its norm is exactly the two-dimensional positive shear norm \(\kappa_p(c)\): the triangle inequality gives the upper bound and a norming sequence for the non-norm-attaining James functional gives the reverse bound. Any norm-attaining vector would force \(|f(y)|=\|y\|\), impossible. Thus \(m(T_c)=\kappa_p(c)^{-1}\) is not attained. For any compact \(K\), \(T_c+K=I+(K-N_c)\) and compact operators on infinite-dimensional spaces are not bounded below, so \(m(T_c+K)\le1\); taking \(K=N_c\) attains 1. The endpoint formula \(\kappa_1(c)=\kappa_\infty(c)=1+c\) and divergence as \(c\to\infty\) follow directly.
